title: Convexity of functions and sets
context: Convexity and convex sets: secants lie above a convex graph; line segments remain in a convex set.
notes: Red segments distinguish failure of convexity, non-strict convexity with boundary segments, and strict convexity. The middle function has a flat interval, and the middle set has flat boundary segments.

title: Linear regression
context: Least-squares fitting of a linear predictor to training pairs.
notes: The fifteen training pairs form an illustrative scalar-feature dataset. The displayed slope is their exact least-squares minimizer, x-star=sum(a_i y_i)/sum(a_i squared), approximately 0.4589392. The red vertical segment is the signed residual y_i−〈a_i,x-star〉 for the marked observation; no intercept is fitted.

title: A linear classifier
context: The parameter x is normal to the decision hyperplane in feature space.
notes: Positive labels lie on the positive-score side and negative labels on the negative-score side. The normal vector is perpendicular to the separating line, with an explicit right-angle marker. The feature-space origin is marked because this homogeneous decision hyperplane passes through it.

title: Classification losses
context: Smooth empirical classification risk and standard margin losses.
notes: Divided the logistic loss by log(2), giving ell(u)=log(1+exp(u))/log(2). This is an upper bound on the displayed zero-one loss and meets it at u=0, where both equal one. Zero margin counts as an error. The hinge loss also equals one there. Updated the chapter loss definition and its derivative consistently; the derivative is the sigmoid divided by log(2).

title: Existence and uniqueness of minimizers
context: An objective can have no minimizer, several minimizers, or a unique minimizer.
notes: The five representative functions retain the original cases. The two no-minimizer examples explicitly distinguish an unbounded infimum, minus infinity, from the finite unattained infimum zero. The exponential curve stays strictly above its horizontal asymptote. Vertical offsets and coordinate scales are schematic.

title: Coercive least squares
context: Full column rank gives a strictly convex quadratic with a unique minimizer.
notes: The bowl depicts the full-column-rank case. Its height may include a nonzero residual at the minimizer; no exact fit is assumed.

title: Least squares with a nontrivial kernel
context: The objective is constant along translations by vectors in the kernel of A.
notes: The trough is flat exactly along the kernel direction. The highlighted affine line represents x-star+ker(A); arrowheads at both ends show that this entire minimizer set is unbounded in both directions.

title: Failure of the secant inequality
context: The graph of a convex function lies below every secant.
notes: Compact exact secant example for nonconvex. The function is .1*x^4-.7*x^2+2, endpoints (-1.8, 1.8), and intermediate point 0. The chord value is 0.78176 and function value 2.0. The chapter caption defines x_t=(1-t)x+ty and ell_t=(1-t)f(x)+t f(y). The red segment is the secant, and its vertical gap shows the defining inequality or its failure.

title: Convexity and the secant inequality
context: The graph of a convex function lies below every secant.
notes: Compact exact secant example for convex. The function is .2*x^2+.6, endpoints (-1.8, 1.8), and intermediate point 0. The chord value is 1.248 and function value 0.6. The chapter caption defines x_t=(1-t)x+ty and ell_t=(1-t)f(x)+t f(y). The red segment is the secant, and its vertical gap shows the defining inequality or its failure.

title: Strict convexity
context: For distinct endpoints and an interior convex combination, the secant inequality is strict.
notes: Compact exact secant example for strictly convex. The function is .2*x^2+.6, endpoints (-1.8, 1.8), and intermediate point 0.6. The chord value is 1.248 and function value 0.672. The chapter caption defines x_t=(1-t)x+ty and ell_t=(1-t)f(x)+t f(y). The red segment is the secant, and its vertical gap shows the defining inequality or its failure.

title: Convexity with an affine interval
context: A convex function need not be strictly convex.
notes: Compact exact secant example for convex, not strict. The function is .2*max(abs(x)-1,0)^2+.6, endpoints (-0.9, 0.9), and intermediate point 0.2. The chord value is 0.6 and function value 0.6. The chapter caption defines x_t=(1-t)x+ty and ell_t=(1-t)f(x)+t f(y). The red segment is the secant, and its vertical gap shows the defining inequality or its failure.

title: The gradient is a vector field
context: The gradient associates a vector in the domain with each evaluation point.
notes: The radial field is shown for f(x)=||x|| squared/2. Each arrow based at a marked point q has displacement exactly q in the same coordinates, hence ends at 2q. The gradient vanishes at the minimizer. The accompanying bowl uses an uncalibrated projection.

title: Stationarity at local extrema
context: Vanishing derivative is necessary at differentiable local minima and maxima.
notes: The exact quartic f(x)=(x^2-1)^2+0.65 has local minima at -1 and 1 and a local maximum at 0. Horizontal tangent segments identify the three stationary points.

title: A stationary point need not be an extremum
context: The first-order necessary condition is not sufficient without convexity.
notes: The exact cubic f(x)=x^3 has a horizontal tangent at zero and a stationary inflection, which is neither a minimum nor a maximum. Plot coordinates have a vertical drawing offset, with the horizontal axis at f=0.

title: Stationarity for a convex objective
context: For differentiable convex functions, a vanishing gradient characterizes global minimizers.
notes: The tangent plane touches the bowl at its minimum and supports the graph from below. The plane is horizontal in the depicted three-dimensional coordinates.

title: PCA and least-squares level sets
context: Covariance axes and quadratic level-set axes have reciprocal widths.
notes: Both panels share the eigenvectors u₁,u₂. The twelve reflection-symmetric points are centered and have empirical covariance eigenvalues λ₁=1 and λ₂=0.325 squared. Every covariance ellipse and quadratic level set is derived from these same eigenvalues, with reciprocal axis ratios. Width annotations sit above the panels so all data points and complete ellipses remain visible. The caption specifies the multiplier used for each family of semiaxes; C/n follows the covariance normalization in the text.

title: A first-order Taylor approximation
context: The affine approximation matches the function and its derivative at the expansion point.
notes: The line is the exact tangent to the representative quadratic at x. Both f(z) and T_x(z) are labeled at their respective marked points, making the vertical Taylor remainder explicit. The tangent value at the selected z is 2.5466.

title: A tangent plane
context: The first-order affine approximation of a differentiable function in two dimensions.
notes: The tangent plane is computed for the displayed representative paraboloid and touches it at the marked point. The graph and its supporting plane are distinct objects.

title: The gradient is orthogonal to a level curve
context: Differentiating f(c(t))=constant gives a zero pairing with the tangent direction.
notes: At the leftmost point of an elliptical level curve, the tangent is vertical and the outward gradient is horizontal. The right-angle marker records orthogonality, not a descent step.

title: Gradients and nested level sets
context: Gradients point in the direction normal to a level set and toward larger values.
notes: The arrows are normals to elliptical level curves, not radial arrows except on the principal axes. Level values increase outward. A separate key identifies the three complete ellipses, and the drawing explicitly states that arrow lengths are schematic: their directions are the mathematical content.

title: Step-size effects in gradient descent
context: The step size controls progress and oscillation along a quadratic objective.
notes: Both trajectories are exact gradient-descent iterates for the displayed quadratic. The larger step oscillates but remains stable because both step sizes lie in (0,2/L), with L=5. The sketch is schematic; no numerical values were legible in it.

title: Exact line search
context: A differentiable interior line-search optimum makes successive gradients orthogonal.
notes: The path uses exact line search for the displayed positive definite quadratic f(x)=(x₁ squared+5x₂ squared)/2. The right-angle marker is computed from consecutive actual steps. The later, shorter steps remain connected as the path approaches the minimizer.

title: The optimal quadratic step size
context: The operator norm of I−τC is controlled by the extreme eigenvalues.
notes: The highlighted curve is the maximum of the two absolute-value branches, with μ and L explicitly identified as the smallest and largest eigenvalues of C. Its minimum is at 2/(L+μ), and h(τ)<1 exactly for 0<τ<2/L. The drawing states its representative ratio L/μ=3; other labels remain symbolic.

title: Quadratic upper and lower bounds
context: Strong convexity and Lipschitz gradient give touching lower and upper quadratic models.
notes: Both bounding quadratics have the same value and gradient as f at x. The lower curvature μ and upper curvature L are ordered correctly on both sides of the expansion point.

title: An unbiased stochastic gradient
context: Uniform sampling of a summand gives the gradient of its arithmetic mean in expectation.
notes: The red dashed vector is the exact arithmetic mean of the three individual gradient vectors. Its endpoint is the centroid of the lightly shaded triangle joining their endpoints. Uniform sampling from {1,2,3} is stated explicitly, which is required for this unbiased estimate of the arithmetic-mean objective.

title: Stochastic gradient trajectories
context: Individual stochastic iterates fluctuate around the overall direction toward a minimizer.
notes: The path and shrinking ellipses preserve the qualitative intent of the sketch. They are illustrative neighborhoods, not confidence regions or a simulated dataset. A dotted continuation separates the last displayed iterate from the target minimizer. Convergence requires the objective, noise, and step-size assumptions developed in the section; step sizes alone do not guarantee it.
